claude.sample_unit: eye examinations (from 110 infants), graded by 11 experts

links.outcome: Expert plus disease diagnosis agreement with reference standard, without vs with AI severity score assistance
links.effect: Weighted κ improved from 0.69 to 0.81; AUC from 0.94 to 0.98 (difference 0.04); AUPR from 0.86 to 0.95 (difference 0.09).
links.quote: Expert agreement improved significantly, from substantial (κ value, 0.69 [0.59, 0.75]) to near perfect (κ value, 0.81 [0.71, 0.86]), when AI-based VSS was integrated.

links.outcome: Clinician diagnostic performance with versus without AI severity score in reading workflow
links.effect: Mean AUC rose from 0.94 to 0.98 (difference 0.04, 95% CI 0.01-0.06); AUPR from 0.86 to 0.95 with AI-based VSS assistance.
links.quote: Additionally, a significant improvement in plus disease discrimination was achieved as measured by mean AUC (from 0.94 [95% CI, 0.92-0.96] to 0.98 [95% CI, 0.96-0.99]; difference, 0.04 [95% CI, 0.01-0.06]) and AUPR (from 0.86 [95% CI, 0.81-0.90] to 0.95 [95% CI, 0.91-0.97]; difference, 0.09 [95% CI, 0.03-0.14]).

unlisted_practices: Providing an AI-generated continuous severity score to reduce interobserver variability among specialists
